extracted.intended_audience: education researchers, K-12 teachers, and school administrators interested in teacher grant writing and support
extracted.subtask_description: A survey-based study and questionnaire framework for identifying motivating factors, obstacles, and needed support/staff development for K-12 teachers who write grant proposals; includes grouping by years taught, number of grants submitted, and funding level and statistical tests of group differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improved Student Learning (Motivating Factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Making a contribution to improved student learning (motivator scale: 4-strong motivator, 3-average motivator, 2-not a motivator, 1-does not apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified by 94% of teachers as a strong motivator; listed as a primary motivating factor for writing grants and used as one of the motivating-factor items in the questionnaire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources for Needed Equipment (Motivating Factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Having the resources to acquire badly needed equipment (motivator scale as above).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified by 91% of teachers as a strong motivator; included as a core motivator item measuring tangible resource needs as a driver for grant writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfaction in Obtaining Funding (Motivating Factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal satisfaction in obtaining grant funding (motivator scale as above).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 67% of teachers rated this as an average or strong motivator; captures intrinsic reward/recognition from successful funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building Professional Reputation (Motivating Factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Building a personal professional reputation as a successful grant writer (motivator scale as above).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included to measure professional/ career-oriented motivation for grant seeking; used alongside other motivators in analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition from the School District (Motivating Factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gaining recognition from the school district and/or school administration (motivator scale as above).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only 26% identified as strong or average motivator overall, but produced significant differences between funding groups: teachers receiving $1000–$5000 rated recognition higher than those receiving $0–$1000 (p < .05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced Teacher Load (Motivating Factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduced teacher load to work on a successful grant (motivator scale as above).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a motivator item to capture workload/time trade-offs that might incentivize or disincentivize grant writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Knowledge of Funding Opportunities (Obstacle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of knowledge of funding opportunities (obstacle scale: 5-an extreme obstacle, 4-great obstacle, 3-medium obstacle, 2-low obstacle, 1-not an obstacle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as the greatest obstacle by respondents (79% rated it extreme/great/average) and showed significant differences by prior funding level (teachers with $0–$1000 perceived this as a greater obstacle than teachers with >$5000; p < .05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Budgeting and Account Management Knowledge (Obstacle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of knowledge of budgeting and account management (obstacle scale as above).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flagged as a substantial obstacle (with group differences in ANOVA; teachers with lower prior funding saw it as a greater obstacle; p < .05 for some comparisons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Encouragement from School Administration (Obstacle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of encouragement from school administration (obstacle scale as above).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrary to some prior studies, 81% identified this as a low or no obstacle in this sample; included to measure administrative culture/encouragement as an obstacle dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Technical Assistance on How to Write Competitive Proposals (Obstacle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of technical assistance in writing grants (obstacle scale as above).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as an obstacle by 56% (extreme/great/average); significant group differences by prior funding level (teachers with $0–$1000 perceived more technical assistance obstacles than teachers with >$5000; p < .01 for some tests).

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems Dealing with School District's Business Office (Obstacle)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to deal with the school district’s business office (obstacle scale as above).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as an operational/administrative obstacle reflecting post-award management friction between teachers and district finance offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increased Workload That Would Prevent Future Grant Writing (Obstacle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Increased workload to the extent that you would not write another grant (obstacle scale as above).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures whether workload from grant activities is a deterrent to future participation; included as part of obstacle battery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central Office Identification of Available Funding (Needed Support)
rubrics_metrics.description: How often do support personnel in the central office identify available funding sources? (5-Very Frequently to 1-Never).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure organizational support for grant identification; a frequency-based support metric included in the questionnaire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Identification of Available Funding (Needed Support)
rubrics_metrics.description: How often does your principal identify available funding sources? (5-Very Frequently to 1-Never).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures school-level leadership support for identifying grant opportunities; analyzed as a needed-support variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantity/Adequacy of Staff Development Received Prior to Grant Writing (Needed Support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the quantity/adequacy of staff development you received prior to writing your grant (5-very adequate to 1-no training).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 76% reported staff development received was adequate or greater, but 99% indicated continued staff development was needed (needed/very needed/essential). This item informs staff development planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty Managing a Grant Through Your School District (Needed Support / Management Difficulty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the difficulty of managing a grant through your school district once funding was obtained (5-very easy to 1-so difficult as to prevent future grant writing; 0-does not apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers with greater prior funding ($1000–$5000 and >$5000) perceived management difficulties as a greater obstacle than teachers with <$1000 (ANOVA p < .01); this item captures post-award management support needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Helpfulness of Support for Grant Writing and Management to Continued Grant Writing (Needed Support)
rubrics_metrics.description: How helpful would support for grant writing and grant management be to continued grant writing? (4-Essential, 3-Very Helpful, 2-Helpful, 1-Not helpful).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess perceived value of support services for sustaining teacher participation in grant activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent grouping variables: years of teaching, number of grants written, level of funding achieved
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers were categorized by years of teaching, number of grants written (frequency categories), and total funding level achieved; these served as independent variables in group comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses (One-Way ANOVA, Duncan Multiple Range Test, t-tests) used these groupings to detect differences in motivating factors, obstacles, and support needs; a significant positive correlation was found between number of grants written and level of prior funding (p < .01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Response scales and scoring conventions used in the questionnaire
rubrics_metrics.description: Motivator scale: 4-strong motivator to 1-does not apply; Obstacle scale: 5-extreme obstacle to 1-not an obstacle; Support frequency: 5-very frequently to 1-never; Staff development adequacy: 5-very adequate to 1-no training; Management difficulty: 5-very easy to 0-does not apply; Helpfulness: 4-essential to 1-not helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These explicit scoring conventions define how responses are quantified for descriptive statistics, ANOVA and correlation analyses reported in the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis standards: One-Way ANOVA, t-tests, significance thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Group differences were tested using One-Way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), with Duncan Multiple Range Test used for some pairwise comparisons; two-tailed t-tests and correlations were used to assess relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance thresholds reported (e.g., p < .05, p < .01) guide interpretation of which differences are considered meaningful between funding-level groups; tables present F ratios, sums of squares, and means/SDs for items.
